editorial.title: 조직 기강 엉망인데, 경찰청장 자리 비워두는 이유 뭔가
editorial.body: (사설) 경찰청장 자리가 9개월째 공석이며 대행 체제가 1년 9개월째 지속되고 있다. 경찰 조직 개혁, 치안 총수 임명, 경찰 기강 해이, 정부 책임 등 문제로 국민 불신이 커지고 있다. |

조직 기강 해이와 경찰 개혁 지연으로 국민 불신이 급증하고 있다.
정부의 책임 있는 인사 결단이 시급한 상황이다.

editorial.stance: 경찰 조직의 공백 장기화는 치안 신뢰도를 훼손하므로 정부의 즉각적인 인사 결정이 필요하다.
editorial.titleTr: Why Leave Police Chief Post Vacant When Department Discipline Is in Shambles?
summaryTr: The position of police commissioner has remained vacant for nine months, with an acting system in place for one year and nine months.
Public distrust is rapidly increasing due to organizational discipline laxity and delays in police reform.
The government needs to make a responsible personnel decision without delay.
editorial.bodyTr: The position of Police Commissioner has remained vacant for nine months, with an acting system now in place for one year and nine months. Public distrust is growing due to issues surrounding police organizational reform, the appointment of the nation's top law enforcement officer, deteriorating police discipline, and government accountability.

summaryTr: Allegations of lobbying by pharmaceutical startup involving Justice Minister nominee Kim Seung-won
Suspicions of improper intervention in MFDS clinical approval through drinking sessions with warrant judge
Controversy spreads over opposition's double standards
editorial.bodyTr: Allegations of lobbying misconduct have surfaced against Kim Seung-won, the nominee for justice minister. The core issues involve a broker's social gathering with a warrant judge and improper intervention in clinical trial approvals through the Food and Drug Administration, along with suspicions of stock price manipulation. While the Kim camp claims they were merely conveying matters of public interest, the opposition is facing double-standard accusations after having previously criticized judges' social gatherings.

summaryTr: Shift in government personnel policy revealed through replacement of chair of presidential committee for national unity
Integration values fading as reshuffle excludes conservatives and moderates in favor of opposition-centered cabinet
Initial state affairs philosophy being altered according to political circumstances
editorials.bodyTr: The dismissal of Lee Seok-yeon, chairman of the Presidential Committee for National Integration, reflects a shift in the government's personnel policy and a fading of the value of national unity. As the government excludes conservative and centrist figures while reshuffling its cabinet with opposition-affiliated personnel at the center, the initial governing philosophy of integration has been distorted to suit political circumstances.

editorials.titleTr: [Editorial] With $25 Trillion Advance Electricity Payment Plan and U.S. Factory Pressure, Semiconductors Become the Punching Bag
summaryTr: Korea Electric Power Corporation prepaid electricity rates, U.S. tariffs, and Labor Ministry guidelines create triple blow for semiconductor industry
Government is increasing corporate burden instead of supporting industry
Urgent need for whole-of-government industrial protection response
editorials.bodyTr: Korea's semiconductor industry is caught in a pinch from all sides—facing demands from Korea Electric Power Corporation for advance electricity payments, tariff pressure from the United States, and uncertain labor guidelines from the Ministry of Employment and Labor. Critics point out that the government is adding to corporate burdens rather than providing adequate support for semiconductors, which serve as a pillar of the economy. The situation calls for a whole-of-government response to protect the industry.

editorial.body: 입력 업데이트 북한군의 군사분계선(MDL) 월선이 반복되고 있다. 북한이 MDL 일대에 도로와 진지를 구축하면서 상습 월선 구간까지 생겼다. 우리 군은 열상감시장비(TOD) 등을 MDL에 가깝게 전진 배치하는 방안을 검토 중이다. 월선 여부를 정확히 식별해 불필요한 경고사격과 오판을 줄이겠다는 취지다. 필요한 조치지만, 묻지 않을 수 없다. 북한군이 자꾸 선을 넘는데 우리는 안 막는 것인가, 못 막는 것인가. 전선지역에서 대규모 병력 투입돼 작업 중인 북한군.[합동참모본부] 문제는 월선이 실수가 아니라는 점이다. 북한은 전방 요새화 작업을 하며 도로와 진지를 만들고 지뢰까지 매설해 병력을 정기적으로 이동시키고 있다. 일부 이동로가 MDL 남쪽을 지나 상습 월선과 경고사격이 반복되는 구조다. 우리 군의 대응도 달라져야 한다. 하지만 그간 군이 보여준 행보는 우려스러웠다. 지난해 말 국방부 관계자가 북한군의 MDL 침범 시 경고사격에 앞서 상황평가를 면밀히 하라고 지시했고, 군 수뇌부도 기계적 대응 대신 상황에 따른 판단을 주문한 사실이 드러났다. 최전방 ‘빈총 경계’ 실태까지 알려지면서 전방 부대가 경고사격을 자제해 온 정황도 알려졌다. 군이 소극적으로 임할수록 상대가 우리 경계 태세를 시험할 가능성은 커진다. 우리 군이 북한과의 충돌 기피에만 몰두했던 것은 아닌지 돌아봐야 한다. 북한은 최근 노동당 규약에서 ‘평화통일’과 ‘민족대단결’ 등 통일 관련 표현을 삭제하며 ‘적대적 두 국가’ 노선을 한층 공식화했다. 대남 통일 노선 폐기와 최전방 요새화가 같은 방향을 가리키고 있다. 가뜩이나 북한은 핵미사일 개발을 강화하는 상황이다. 이런 북한을 상대로 우리 군이 최전방의 경계를 느슨하게 하는 것은 우리 스스로 안보의 둑을 허무는 일이 된다. 감시장비 전진 배치만으로는 부족하다. 북한의 MDL 침범을 용인하지 않겠다는 원칙을 분명히 하고, 유엔군사령부와 감시·대응 체계도 긴밀히 조율해야 한다. 강신철 국방부 장관 후보자는 취임 후 MDL 문제를 최우선 현안으로 삼아 흐트러진 군의 기강과 느슨해진 대북 경계 태세를 바로잡아야 할 것이다. 안보는 말이나 양보가 아니라 단호한 원칙과 압도적 대응력으로 지키는 것이다.

editorial.titleTr: North Korea Breaches MDL at Will — Can It Be Stopped?
summaryTr: North Korean forces are habitually breaching the MDL, constructing roads and fortifications.
Concerns have been raised that our military has loosened its vigilance by focusing solely on avoiding confrontation.
Surveillance equipment deployment alone is insufficient; clear principles and firm responses are needed.
editorial.bodyTr:
North Korean troops repeatedly cross the Military Demarcation Line (MDL). As North Korea constructs roads and fortifications around the MDL, habitual crossing points have emerged. Our military is reviewing plans to deploy forward thermal observation devices (TOD) and other surveillance equipment closer to the MDL. The aim is to accurately identify crossings and reduce unnecessary warning shots and misjudgments. While a necessary measure, the question demands to be asked: Is our military failing to stop North Korean crossings, or unable to stop them?

The problem is that these crossings are not accidents. North Korea is conducting large-scale fortification work along the front, constructing roads and fortifications, laying mines, and regularly moving troops. Some movement routes pass south of the MDL, creating a recurring pattern of habitual crossings and warning fire. Our military's response must change accordingly. However, the military's recent conduct has been concerning. It was revealed that a Defense Ministry official last year ordered careful situational assessment before warning shots in response to North Korean MDL violations, and military leadership also instructed judgment based on circumstances rather than mechanical responses. As reports emerged of frontline units maintaining a "weapons-unloaded" posture, it became clear that forward troops have been exercising restraint in firing warning shots. The more passively our military acts, the more likely the other side will test our defensive readiness. We must reconsider whether our military has been focused solely on avoiding confrontation with North Korea. North Korea recently deleted phrases related to reunification such as "peaceful unification" and "ethnic solidarity" from its Workers' Party charter, further formalizing its "hostile two-state" policy line. The abandonment of inter-Korean unification policy and frontline fortification point in the same direction. This comes as North Korea intensifies nuclear and missile development. For our military to loosen vigilance at the frontlines against such a North Korea amounts to dismantling our own security defenses. Forward deployment of surveillance equipment alone is insufficient. We must firmly establish the principle of not tolerating North Korean MDL violations and closely coordinate surveillance and response systems with the United Nations Command. Defense Minister nominee Shin Shin-chul must make the MDL issue his top priority upon taking office and correct the military's laxened discipline and weakened posture toward North Korea. Security is protected not through words or concessions but through steadfast principle and overwhelming deterrence.

editorial.title: Hollow reforms
editorial.body: Political caution weakens pension overhaul, leaving future generations with rising costs In South Korea, the basic pension has a curious tendency to become less ambitious as it approaches the ballot box. The closer a proposed overhaul gets to voters, the smaller it seems to become. The Lee Jae Myung administration began with an ambitious promise to make the basic pension “heavier at the bottom and lighter at the top” in terms of benefits. On Tuesday, however, the government delivered a much narrower change. It kept the politically convenient 70 percent coverage rule and made only limited adjustments to payouts. Korea faces a difficult pension dilemma: protecting a growing number of impoverished elderly people without allowing public finances to buckle under demographic pressure. The latest plan handles the first concern at the margins and largely postpones the second. Under the new scheme starting next April, monthly payouts for the bottom 30 percent will rise to 380,000 won ($279), while the 30 to 45 percent bracket will receive an inflation-adjusted 359,000 won. Payments for the upper 45 to 70 percent remain frozen at 350,000 won, and the spousal reduction for lower-income couples will ease from 20 to 10 percent. That is a modest redistribution within an expanding system. Freezing payments for the upper tier saves about 170 billion won, while differentiated payouts require an additional 465 billion won. The annual basic pension budget will consequently rise by about 11 percent, from 23.1 trillion won this year to 25.7 trillion won next year. The compromise is especially conspicuous because the Ministry of Health and Welfare had considered replacing the 70 percent rule with a median-income threshold, eventually reducing eligibility to 80 percent by 2030. After a scheduled briefing by Health and Welfare Minister Jeong Eun-kyeong was abruptly canceled on Aug. 27, however, the final proposal dropped eligibility reform altogether. The political logic is hardly mysterious. With public sentiment already unsettled by real estate tax changes and the president’s approval ratings weakening, reducing pension eligibility would have imposed another immediate political cost. The 70 percent rule has become harder to justify as a proxy for need. Some older single workers earning around 4.68 million won a month can qualify if they have no other assets, while married couples with combined annual income approaching 100 million won may also fall within the threshold. Meanwhile, Korea still has one of the highest elderly poverty rates in the OECD. Adding 30,000 won a month to the poorest group will hardly transform that picture, particularly when basic pension payments can interact awkwardly with minimum livelihood benefits. Then comes the demographic ledger. Basic pension recipients have grown from about 2 million in 2015 to 7.79 million this year. Their number is projected to reach 13.3 million by 2050, while spending could rise to 46 trillion won, according to the Korea Development Institute. That trajectory demands a clearer definition of whom the basic pension is meant to support. Eligibility should gradually move toward an objective median-income benchmark rather than a fixed share of the elderly population. Savings from narrower coverage should be redirected toward seniors facing genuine hardship. The system should also evolve alongside the maturing national pension fund and voluntary private retirement savings. The Lee administration has postponed the difficult part of reform. That may ease political friction for the moment, but demographic arithmetic does not disappear because it chooses to defer it. Sustainability cannot be achieved by passing a diluted bill. Preserving broad entitlements while gutting core reforms is a compromise in name only, leaving future generations to settle the bill. S. summaryTr: 남한의 연금 개혁안이 유권자 투표를 앞두고 야심을 줄이며 정치적으로 편리한 규칙들을 유지하고 있다.
이 안은 가장 가난한 노인들의 급여를 적당히 인상하지만 장기적 지속 가능성을 위해 필요한 더 어려운 수급 자격 제한을 피하고 있다.
기초연금 수급자는 2050년까지 1330만 명으로 급증할 것이지만, 미루어진 개혁들은 미래 세대가 비용을 치르도록 남긴다.
editorial.bodyTr:
정치적 신중함이 연금 개혁을 약화시키며 미래 세대에 증가하는 비용 부담을 남기다

한국에서 기초연금은 투표에 가까워질수록 덜 야심 차기 되는 기묘한 경향을 보인다. 개혁안이 유권자에게 가까워질수록 그 규모는 작아지는 것 같다. 이재명 정부는 기초연금의 혜택을 "아래는 무겁게, 위는 가볍게" 만들겠다는 야심 찬 공약으로 시작했다. 그러나 지난 화요일 정부가 발표한 것은 훨씬 더 제한적인 변화였다. 정치적으로 편리한 70% 보장 원칙을 유지한 채 급여 조정만 제한적으로 했다.

한국은 어려운 연금의 딜레마에 직면해 있다. 증가하는 빈곤층 노인을 보호하면서도 인구 감소 압력으로 인한 재정 파탄을 막아야 한다는 것이다. 최신 계획은 첫 번째 우려사항에는 제한적으로 대응하고 두 번째 문제는 대부분 미루고 있다.

상위층 급여 동결로 약 1,700억 원이 절감되는 반면, 차등 지급에는 추가로 4,650억 원이 필요하다. 따라서 기초연금 연간 예산은 올해 23조 1천억 원에서 내년 25조 7천억 원으로 약 11% 증가할 것이다.

이번 타협이 특히 눈에 띄는 이유는 보건복지부가 70% 원칙을 중위소득 기준으로 대체하여 2030년까지 적용 대상을 80%로 줄이는 방안을 검토했기 때문이다. 그러나 정경은 보건복지부 장관의 8월 27일 예정된 브리핑이 갑자기 취소된 후, 최종 제안에서는 적용 대상 개혁이 완전히 빠졌다.

정치적 논리는 거의 명백하다. 부동산세 변화로 국민 감정이 불안정한 상황에서 대통령 지지율도 약해지고 있는 가운데, 연금 적용 대상을 줄이는 것은 또 다른 즉각적인 정치적 비용을 초래했을 것이다.

70% 원칙은 필요성의 척도로서 점점 더 정당화하기 어려워졌다. 월소득이 약 468만 원인 고령 단독 가구자도 다른 자산이 없으면 대상이 될 수 있고, 연 소득이 약 1억 원에 가까운 기혼 부부도 기준을 충족할 수 있다. 한편 한국은 여전히 OECD 국가 중 노인 빈곤율이 높은 국가 중 하나다. 가장 빈곤한 계층에 월 3만 원을 더하는 것은 특히 기초연금 지급이 최저생계비 보조와 어색하게 상호작용할 수 있을 때 그 상황을 크게 개선하지 못할 것이다.

그 다음은 인구통계학적 계산이다. 기초연금 수급자는 2015년 약 200만 명에서 올해 779만 명으로 증가했다. 한국개발연구원에 따르면 수급자 수는 2050년까지 1,330만 명에 이를 것으로 예상되고, 지출은 46조 원에 이를 수 있다. 이러한 궤적은 기초연금이 누구를 지원하기 위한 것인지에 대한 더 명확한 정의를 요구한다.

적용 대상을 고령 인구의 고정된 비율보다는 객관적 중위소득 기준으로 점진적으로 이동해야 한다. 더 좁은 적용 범위에서 나오는 절감액은 진정한 어려움에 처한 노인을 향해 재투자되어야 한다. 이 체계는 또한 성숙해가는 국민연금기금 및 자발적 민간 퇴직연금저축과 함께 진화해야 한다.

editorials.title: Hollow reforms
editorials.body: Political caution weakens pension overhaul, leaving future generations with rising costs In South Korea, the basic pension has a curious tendency to become less ambitious as it approaches the ballot box. The closer a proposed overhaul gets to voters, the smaller it seems to become. The Lee Jae Myung administration began with an ambitious promise to make the basic pension “heavier at the bottom and lighter at the top” in terms of benefits. On Tuesday, however, the government delivered a much narrower change. It kept the politically convenient 70 percent coverage rule and made only limited adjustments to payouts. Korea faces a difficult pension dilemma: protecting a growing number of impoverished elderly people without allowing public finances to buckle under demographic pressure. The latest plan handles the first concern at the margins and largely postpones the second. Under the new scheme starting next April, monthly payouts for the bottom 30 percent will rise to 380,000 won ($279), while the 30 to 45 percent bracket will receive an inflation-adjusted 359,000 won. Payments for the upper 45 to 70 percent remain frozen at 350,000 won, and the spousal reduction for lower-income couples will ease from 20 to 10 percent. That is a modest redistribution within an expanding system. Freezing payments for the upper tier saves about 170 billion won, while differentiated payouts require an additional 465 billion won. The annual basic pension budget will consequently rise by about 11 percent, from 23.1 trillion won this year to 25.7 trillion won next year. The compromise is especially conspicuous because the Ministry of Health and Welfare had considered replacing the 70 percent rule with a median-income threshold, eventually reducing eligibility to 80 percent by 2030. After a scheduled briefing by Health and Welfare Minister Jeong Eun-kyeong was abruptly canceled on Aug. 27, however, the final proposal dropped eligibility reform altogether. The political logic is hardly mysterious. With public sentiment already unsettled by real estate tax changes and the president’s approval ratings weakening, reducing pension eligibility would have imposed another immediate political cost. The 70 percent rule has become harder to justify as a proxy for need. Some older single workers earning around 4.68 million won a month can qualify if they have no other assets, while married couples with combined annual income approaching 100 million won may also fall within the threshold. Meanwhile, Korea still has one of the highest elderly poverty rates in the OECD. Adding 30,000 won a month to the poorest group will hardly transform that picture, particularly when basic pension payments can interact awkwardly with minimum livelihood benefits. Then comes the demographic ledger. Basic pension recipients have grown from about 2 million in 2015 to 7.79 million this year. Their number is projected to reach 13.3 million by 2050, while spending could rise to 46 trillion won, according to the Korea Development Institute. That trajectory demands a clearer definition of whom the basic pension is meant to support. Eligibility should gradually move toward an objective median-income benchmark rather than a fixed share of the elderly population. Savings from narrower coverage should be redirected toward seniors facing genuine hardship. The system should also evolve alongside the maturing national pension fund and voluntary private retirement savings. The Lee administration has postponed the difficult part of reform. That may ease political friction for the moment, but demographic arithmetic does not disappear because it chooses to defer it. Sustainability cannot be achieved by passing a diluted bill. Preserving broad entitlements while gutting core reforms is a compromise in name only, leaving future generations to settle the bill. S. editorial.bodyTr: The government has issued administrative guidelines stating that performance bonuses linked to operating profit and business management decisions such as artificial intelligence implementation are not subjects of labor disputes. editorials.bodyTr: Kim Seung-won, the nominee for justice minister, stated on the 3rd regarding the withdrawal of charges in President Lee Jae-myung's case that "the justice minister does not have direct authority, and I have no intention to direct the prosecutor general." Amid fierce attacks from the People Power Party and others labeling Kim as a "minister for dropping charges," Kim has taken a principled stance of distancing himself from political interference in prosecution matters. However, questions persist about whether such a position can be maintained given the sensitive nature of the case and the political pressures surrounding the appointment. The justice minister's office traditionally maintains a formal separation from prosecutorial decisions, though the reality of influence through indirect channels has long been a point of contention in Korean politics. Kim's explicit renunciation of any directive role toward the prosecutor general appears designed to preempt accusations of politicizing the justice system, yet critics argue that the very act of appointing a justice minister amid such circumstances invites scrutiny about motives. The nominee's commitment to procedural propriety will face its first test once he assumes office, as the Lee case and related matters continue to draw intense public attention and political debate.

editorials.title: [사설] 공공기관 통폐합·지방 이전, 방향 맞더라도 신중한 접근 필요
editorials.body: [사설] 공공기관 통폐합·지방 이전, 방향 맞더라도 신중한 접근 필요, 오피니언
editorials.pullQuote: 공공기관 통폐합·지방 이전, 방향 맞더라도 신중한 접근 필요
summary: 공공기관 통폐합과 지방 이전은 방향이 맞지만 신중한 접근이 필요하다.
무리한 추진은 조직 혼란과 서비스 공백을 초래할 수 있다.
단계적이고 체계적인 계획 수립이 선행되어야 한다.
editorials.stance: 정책 방향은 타당하나 신중하고 체계적인 이행이 필수다
editorials.titleTr: Editorial: Public Agency Consolidation and Relocation Need Careful Approach Despite Right Direction
summaryTr: The consolidation of public institutions and their relocation to provincial areas are directionally correct, but a cautious approach is necessary.
Reckless implementation could result in organizational chaos and gaps in service delivery.
Phased and systematic planning must be established first.
